details: CONFIRMED by count and by reading working-with-me.md. Rated MEDIUM under the project's waste principle (cost
repeated in every session's context) and because it departs from two explicit lines of the brief, the contract.
Trim candidates: section 8 Do, the repeated "say it in one line" in section 2, the long Do of section 1.
evidence: rules/working-with-me.md: "Every question opens with an introduction: what it is about, how the mechanism works,
a live example ... and what each answer changes"; "Name things by what they do for me, not by internal names".
failing_case: `sed 1,2d rules/principles.md | wc -w` prints 904; the brief asks "About 600-700 words". Section 8's Do line
("add the introduction (mechanism, live example, what each answer changes), replace names with what they do")
repeats rules/working-with-me.md lines on question introductions and on naming things by what they do, while the
brief says "do not duplicate what it already says; section 8 adds only the signal". Section 2's Do also repeats
the intro's "say it in one line with its number". The whole text is loaded into every relay session (and every
opting-in project's session), so the excess repeats on every run.
fix_hint: Cut section 8's Do to "apply Working with me before sending; estimates in agent minutes and percent of limit";
drop the repeated "say it in one line with its number" from section 2's Do; tighten section 1's Do.
pass_cases: 1. `sed 1,2d rules/principles.md | wc -w` prints at most about 720.
2. Section 8 has a "Fires on:" line and a Do that only points at Working with me plus what it lacks (estimates in
agent minutes and percent of limit); it no longer lists the introduction's parts or "replace names".
3. The waste section still contains "waste that repeats on every run or every change is MEDIUM" (test asserts it).
4. All nine "## <n>. " headings still render in the relay target (TestPrinciplesRule passes).
findings.summary: the rule is 904 words against the brief's 600-700, and section 8's Do restates Working with me, which the brief forbids

details: CONFIRMED by reading the draft and the rule. LOW: a compaction choice, but it removes the signal behind the
section's own motivating case. Size: 5 agent minutes.
evidence: draft section 1 "Когда срабатывает": "...порядок, названный владельцем, расходится с тем, что делается."
draft: "Новые возможности — по числу важности (IP), которое задаёт владелец"
failing_case: The draft's section 1 fires on "порядок, названный владельцем, расходится с тем, что делается" and orders new
features by the owner's IP (an agent-chosen IP is marked as such); its live example is the owner's "guard and gate
first after the trial" overtaken by other merges. rules/principles.md line 8 lists only "two items compete; a
defect put off; a check skipped", and the Do says "if the order does not decide, ask" without naming IP, though
every .relay/queue item carries "ip". A front that takes a lower-IP item, or ignores an order the owner stated,
gets no signal from this rule.
fix_hint: Add the owner-order signal to Fires on and "new work by the owner's IP" to the rule line, within the word bound.
pass_cases: 1. Section 1's Fires on includes "the order the owner named differs from what is being done".
2. Section 1 says new work is ranked by the owner's importance number (IP), and an IP an agent chose is marked so.
3. The word count still meets F1's bound.
findings.summary: section 1 drops the draft's signal 'the order the owner named differs from what is being done' and the IP ordering of new work

details: CONFIRMED by rendering. LOW: readable today, structure unclear. Size: 5 agent minutes.
evidence: python3 -c "...render_target('relay', ...)" headings: "## Principles", "## 1. Order: what comes first", ...
failing_case: Rendering the relay target prints "# Principles this project loads", "## Principles", "## 1. Order...",
... "## 9. Decide...": the sections are siblings of the rule heading. A project that loads principles with
openspec and quality-gate gets "## OpenSpec", "## 1. Order", ..., "## Quality gate" at one level, so the nine
sections read as separate rules. rules/front.md uses "###" for its subsection (Compact Instructions).
fix_hint: Change the nine "## n." headings to "### n.".
pass_cases: 1. Rendering the relay target prints "## Principles" followed by "### 1. Order: what comes first" ... "### 9. ...".
2. TestPrinciplesRule still passes (its assertIn("## {n}. ") matches "### n. ").
findings.summary: the nine sections use '##', so in a rendered CLAUDE file they sit beside the rule's own '## Principles' and beside other rules

details: Question for the owner. Intro: the principles rule turns the draft's nine sections into instructions every relay
agent follows. The draft flagged one line as the author's inference, not the owner's decision: when the owner asks
"why not do X?", the agent answers with a recommendation and acts only after the owner's word. Live example: three
past "why not" questions (decisions 29, 51, 55) were carried out as orders. Answer (a) keep: such questions get an
answer first, then wait; (b) drop: agents use judgement on each "why not". The owner said the sections "suit me",
which may already cover it. Size: 5 agent minutes either way.
evidence: draft section 9: "предположение Вопрос владельца вида «почему бы не…» (№ 29, 51, 55) — это вопрос, а не указание
failing_case: The draft marks this line "предположение ... Опирается на 0 решений владельца" and says the decisions page asks the
owner about it. rules/principles.md line 50 states it as a rule with no mark. If the owner meant a "why not X?" as
"do X", agents now answer and wait instead of doing it.
fix_hint: Ask the owner; keep or drop the sentence accordingly.
pass_cases: 1. Either the owner confirms the line (it stays), or it is removed / marked until confirmed.
findings.summary: section 9's 'a why-not from the owner is a question, not an order' was marked in the draft as an assumption resting on no owner decision; the rule states it as settled

notes: Fine: projects.toml load/skip swap; render_target raises on an unknown rule, so no target still names taste
(none does); the global render drops the rule from "read when they apply" and keeps the other five (test asserts
it and fails if skip is removed); waste section keeps taste's substance and severity rule verbatim; no project
names, dated examples or owner quotes in the rule; the 5-merge experiment wording is gone with rules/taste.md.
The brief's premise that roles/judge.md and generated agents point at the taste rule was wrong: on master every
"taste" there is "a matter of taste" (a different sense) or the look-review TASTE verdict, so nothing needed
changing and Assembly produced no diff. That is correct, not a gap.
After the merge `relay sync` must run: ~/relay/CLAUDE.local.md still carries the taste text until then
docs/handover.md still speaks of taste; it is the front's record and outside this change.
